models.name: discussion_board_system_settings
models.description:
Platform-wide configuration and placeholder for systematic board settings.

This model holds system-level settings, toggles, or infrastructure parameters that may affect platform-wide policy, appearance, or technical operation. It allows for minimal, future-proof configuration management, ensuring the backend can support extension or modification without schema disruption.

Initially designed as a placeholder, this table supports single or multiple business-defined settings through a key/value pattern. All change events (creation, updates, and deletion) are tracked for audit and rollback. The model enables admins or operators to programmatically control or audit system-wide states, without duplicating config in other domain schemas.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for the system settings entry.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for this configuration setting or policy entry. Used to retrieve or update specific settings programmatically.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Value for this system setting. May encode raw value, serialized JSON, or application-specific policy text.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional human-readable explanation or policy summary for this setting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for creation of this settings entry.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for last update or modification.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit and rollback; null unless marked for deletion.

models.name: discussion_board_users
models.description:
User accounts for platform participants.

Represents each registered end-user on the discussion board. Contains identity fields for login, authentication, account status, and minimal profile information. Every user may have multiple concurrent active sessions tracked in the discussion_board_user_sessions table. Business logic ensures email is unique for secure login. Temporal fields enable soft deletion and audit trails. Fields facilitate account recovery and future extensibility for additional user profile attributes.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Universally unique identifier for the user.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address for login and notification purposes. Must be unique. Used for authentication and password recovery.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Secure hash of the user's password. Used for authentication. Plain passwords are never stored.

plainFields.name: is_email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the user's email address has been verified. Email verification is required before participation.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Denotes if the user account is active and allowed to log in. Blocked users have this set to false.

plainFields.name: is_blocked
plainFields.description: Indicates if the user is blocked for rule violations. Blocked users cannot log in or participate until reactivated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp for soft deletion. If set, the account is considered deleted but can be restored.

models.name: discussion_board_user_sessions
models.description:
Session records for user authentication.

Tracks each login session established by a user. Enables multiple concurrent sessions for a single user (multi-device support). Stores IP and contextual metadata for audits and access control. Sessions are associated with discussion_board_users via a foreign key. Expired sessions are notable for audit and security purposes. No other business data is stored in this subsidiary table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Universally unique identifier for the session.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the associated user account. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL from which the login or session was established.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer value at the start of the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Time the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Time the session expired or ended, nullable until session ends.

models.name: discussion_board_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts for platform oversight and moderation.

Stores credentials and status flags for admin users who govern the discussion board. Admins are promoted from the user base by operators and have enhanced privileges for moderation, content management, and account control. Email addresses must be unique for proper authentication. Admins feature the same authentication and status patterns as regular users but are managed in a distinct, secured table. Soft deletion and audit fields help maintain compliance and traceability for admin actions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Universally unique identifier for the admin.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Admin's unique email address used for login and communication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Secure hash of the admin's password for authentication.

plainFields.name: is_email_verified
plainFields.description: Indicates if the admin's email address has been verified.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: True if admin account is active and enabled for moderation activity.

plainFields.name: is_blocked
plainFields.description: True if the admin is suspended or blocked from accessing admin features.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the admin's profile or status.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of soft deletion; nullable if the account is not deleted.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_sessions
models.description:
Session records for administrator authentication and moderation tracking.

Stores all admin login sessions, supporting audit trails and concurrent multi-device moderation. Each session references the corresponding admin in the discussion_board_admins table. Tracks connection context and session lifecycle. Sessions are removed or expired for security and operational management. Essential for logging admin actions and maintaining platform integrity.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key. Universally unique identifier for the admin session.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the associated admin account. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Network IP address for this moderation session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL at start of session or moderation activity.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer value for admin connection context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation time.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session end time, nullable until expired.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Discussion board articles representing user- or admin-authored posts as primary content for economic and political debate.

Each article contains essential business data such as title and body, subject to length limits and business rules described in requirements. Articles are attributed to the creating user or admin. File and image attachments are handled via a separate table. Articles are the main entry point for debate, searchable by title or content. Edits and deletions are fully audit-trailed by related snapshot and moderation tables. Removal will cascade to attachments and comments.

foreignFields.name: author_user_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reference to the user who authored this article. Null if authored by an admin. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: author_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Optional reference to the admin who authored this article. Null if authored by a user. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article headline. Required. Must be between 5 and 150 characters.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Main content of the article. Must be between 20 and 5000 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when article was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when article was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_article_attachments
models.description:
Attachments associated with articles, such as images or documents, supporting evidence-based discussion.

Each attachment is directly tied to a single article. Allowed file types and size limits are enforced at business logic layer. Attachments are stored as URIs referencing backend storage locations. Deletion of the parent article cascades to attachments.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: uri
plainFields.description: Storage URI for the file or image attachment.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original filename of the uploaded attachment.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the attachment, as checked on upload.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of attachment in bytes. Enforced maximum 10MB via business rules.

plainFields.name: uploaded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded.

models.name: discussion_board_article_snapshots
models.description:
Historical snapshots of article states for versioning, edit trails, and audit purposes.

Stores a copy of article content, title, and author information at each versioning event. New snapshot records are created whenever an article is edited. Snapshots ensure a complete edit history for compliance, moderation, and rollback analysis. Snapshots are never modified or deleted outside of full article or system purge events.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article whose state this snapshot captures. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: author_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user author at the time of this snapshot. Nullable if authored or modified by admin. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: author_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the admin author at the time of this snapshot. Nullable if authored/modified by user. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Snapshot of the article title at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Snapshot of the main article content at the snapshot time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the snapshot was created.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Commentary created by registered users or administrators on discussion board articles.

Each comment is associated with a specific article. Comments can be authored by either normal users or admins, linked by foreign keys. The content of each comment is subject to length validations and may include up to 2 attached files managed via subsidiary attachments table.

Comments are visible under their parent article and support creation, editing, and deletion by their owner (user or admin) as well as by administrators for moderation. When an article is deleted, all its comments are deleted as well. Comment deletions are implemented as soft deletes for traceability and moderation audit.

Comment creation and modification times are recorded for sorting and review. Provides the central entity for all discussion under articles.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article to which this comment belongs. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_user_id
foreignFields.description: User author of the comment, if authored by a regular user. Nullable for admin-authored comments. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin author of the comment, if authored by an admin. Nullable for user-authored comments. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: The content text of the comment. Subject to business validation (2-1000 characters).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last edited.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion time. Set when the comment is removed for user or moderation reasons.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_attachments
models.description:
Files or images attached to a comment on the discussion board.

Each record links a single file/image to one parent comment. Used to manage comment attachment uploads (max two per comment). Only attachments of allowed types and sizes may be added per business validation.

Attachment entities are always dependent on their parent comment and deleted when the parent is deleted. Includes information needed to implement download authorization (only for authenticated users), as well as metadata for moderation and auditing.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: file_url
plainFields.description: Storage location URI for the attachment file.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: The filename as originally uploaded by the user.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the attachment (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf').

plainFields.name: file_size_bytes
plainFields.description: The file size in bytes. Enforced as max 10MB by business rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was created/uploaded.

models.name: discussion_board_reports
models.description:
User-submitted moderation reports tracking flagged content or abusive behavior.

This table captures all reported cases by users regarding articles, comments, or attachments requiring moderation or review. Each report includes metadata for the reporter (user), the type and ID of the entity reported, the nature of the report (reason/category), and the processing status. Only authenticated users may submit reports, and every report is associated with the precise timestamp of its creation.

The moderation team uses this table to review, resolve, or escalate reported incidents, providing an audit trail for transparency and compliance. All content and user references point to existing normalized tables. Deletion is soft to maintain historical audit integrity.

foreignFields.name: reporter_user_id
foreignFields.description: Reporter user account that created the moderation report. {@link discussion_board_users.id}.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity being reported (e.g., 'article', 'comment', 'attachment'). Used to distinguish the context of the moderation report.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: ID of the reported entity (referencing articles, comments, or attachments depending on target_type). Not a foreign key due to multi-entity polymorphism, but always references business entities.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason or category provided for the report (e.g., spam, abuse, illegal content).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Additional details or user explanation for the report. Optional extended text field for further clarification.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the report (e.g., open, in_review, resolved, rejected, escalated).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the report was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent update or review of the report.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if not deleted; set when report is removed for business or compliance reasons.

models.name: discussion_board_moderation_logs
models.description:
Audit trail for all moderation and administrative actions performed by platform admins.

This table records every explicit moderation or admin action on user content, including edits, deletions, warnings, user suspensions, and others. Each log includes references to the admin who performed the action, the type of entity targeted, the specific target entity ID, a code describing the action (e.g., 'delete', 'edit', 'suspend'), freeform notes, and timestamps.

Log records are immutable business events and form the foundation for auditability, compliance, and future incident review. All admin and content references point to pre-existing, normalized entities. Deletion is soft to allow for complete audit history even when entries are hidden from routine views.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed this moderation action. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity or user subjected to moderation action (e.g., 'article', 'comment', 'user', 'attachment').

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: ID of the entity or user affected by admin action. Polymorphic reference; resolved at application level based on target_type.

plainFields.name: action_code
plainFields.description: Code or keyword for the action performed (e.g., 'delete', 'edit', 'restore', 'suspend', 'warn').

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description: Optional additional explanation or notes from the admin about the action taken.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this moderation action was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to log entry (if any corrections or updates are made).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if log entry is active; set for hidden or expunged from casual display, never hard-deleted for audit purposes.
